name: Bima USBD
oneLiner: USBD is Bima's Bitcoin-backed CDP stablecoin minted from overcollateralized BTC LST vaults under Liquity-style mechanics with a USDC/USDP/GUSD PSM.
collateral: Bitcoin liquid staking/restaking derivatives and other approved BTC wrappers deposited into BIMA vaults; the Peg Stability Module can also hold approved stablecoins such as USDC, USDP, and GUSD for peg operations
pegMechanism: Liquity-style overcollateralized vaults with a 150% minimum collateral ratio; USBD can be redeemed permissionlessly for $1 of BTC-denominated collateral from the lowest-ratio vaults with a fee of coreRate + 75 bps; a Peg Stability Module adds near-1:1 USDC/USDP/GUSD swaps

oracleRisk.summary: Bima's documented USBD collateral markets use listed external oracle contracts through a shared PriceFeed that rejects stale, invalid, or greater-than-50% round changes, retains the last valid price only within the configured heartbeat, and otherwise reverts price-dependent operations.

branchApplicability.rationale: Bima deploys a distinct TroveManager for each collateral while sharing the same PriceFeed, LiquidationManager, and multi-collateral Stability Pool implementation. The official address registry maps the documented collateral markets to their external oracle contracts, so the markets are reviewed as one grouped common-engine branch with every listed active TroveManager collateral enumerated.

branches.label: Documented Bima EVM TroveManager markets
branches.summary: Nine collateral markets with published TroveManager and oracle addresses use Bima's common Liquity-derived liquidation engine and multi-collateral Stability Pool across Ethereum, Hemi, Plume, Sonic, GOAT, BSC, and Nibiru.

feeds.path: BTC/USD for Ethereum WBTC, tacBTC, and strBTC

branches.fallbackBehavior: PriceFeed accepts a new external-oracle round only when the current and previous responses are valid, the current response is within the configured per-token heartbeat, and the round-to-round change is at most 50%. Otherwise it returns the stored last valid price only while that record remains within the heartbeat; after that it reverts rather than switching providers.
branches.liquidationMechanism: Any external actor may immediately call the shared LiquidationManager for an eligible Trove. Below MCR, USBD in the Stability Pool offsets debt and depositors receive collateral; any debt and collateral not offset are redistributed to remaining active Troves, with Recovery Mode adding liquidations below system TCR.
branches.backstop: The multi-collateral Stability Pool is the first liquidation backstop. It burns deposited USBD against eligible Trove debt and credits the seized collateral to depositors; any portion beyond pool capacity is redistributed across active Troves in the same collateral market.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: During collateral sunsetting, new loans are disabled and Stability Pool collateral handoff is disabled, so liquidations redistribute debt and collateral to remaining active Troves. The LiquidationManager preserves one final Trove per market by design, and the reviewed contracts do not define a separate global settlement or external bad-debt fund.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-reviewed 2026-07-22: DebtToken.burn(account, amount) is callable by enabled TroveManagers and the owner-configured lending-vault adapter without holder allowance. Those protocol-authorized paths can destroy an arbitrary holder balance, so true replaces the prior inherited-only posture. The same DebtToken address is tracked across deployments.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USBD is a native LayerZero Omnichain Fungible Token (OFT): its verified Ethereum DebtToken source imports @layerzerolabs/oft-evm/contracts/OFT.sol and is declared `contract DebtToken is OFT`, taking a LayerZero V2 endpoint in its constructor (send/quoteSend/lzReceive/setPeer present), so cross-chain supply moves via burn-on-source / mint-on-destination over LayerZero messaging — a regular OFT, not a lockbox adapter or a third-party liquidity bridge (the L2BEAT 'Across' reference is just a bridge that can route USBD, not its issuance path). Re-verified on-chain 2026-07-20: all six tracked deployments are a byte-identical 19,637-byte DebtToken OFT at the same CREATE2 address 0x6bede1c6009a78c222d9bdb7974bb67847fdb68c; endpoint() returns the LayerZero EndpointV2 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fe728c on ethereum/bsc and chain-specific LayerZero endpoints on hemi and sonic (0x6f475642a6e85809b1c36fa62763669b1b48dd5b, eid() 30329/30332), nibiru (0x2a5e79dee6e3544588bb3b675b1cc3354df2aefd, eid 30369), and plume (0xc1b15d3b262beec0e3565c11c9e0f6134bdacb36, eid 30370); owner() is the same documented EOA 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4 on all six chains (eth_getCode = 0 on ethereum; the OFT owner/delegate reviewed under mintAuthority). OFT peer wiring is sparse: peers() on the ethereum token returns non-zero only for sonic (30332) and plume (30370). Native CDP minting via BorrowerOperations exists per chain (reviewed on ethereum 2026-07-14; Bima registry also lists markets on hemi/plume/sonic/bsc/nibiru). Per-application DVN security stack remains unreviewed, so cross-chain routes stay external-validated-network. DefiLlama additionally reports USBD supply under the raw chain labels GOAT and CORE, which do not canonicalize to any CHAIN_META entry — a policy-maintainer-routed label pool, not fixable from coin data.

mintAuthority.summary: USBD is a multichain Liquity-v1-fork CDP. Ethereum and the larger Hemi deployment use the same BorrowerOperations, Factory, BimaCore, and DebtToken addresses. Native CDP issuance is collateral/cap-limited, but one shared BimaCore owner EOA can mint directly without limit, install new mint adapters or TroveManagers, and raise ceilings; a separate EOA controls LayerZero OFT peers.

controls.label: BIMA BorrowerOperations (Liquity-v1 fork)
controls.capDescription: Mint gated by per-collateral debt ceilings and a 150% minimum collateral ratio enforced by the TroveManager/Factory.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712273, DebtToken.borrowerOperationsAddress() still returned this contract; BorrowerOperations.owner() and its Factory/BIMA_CORE chain still resolved to the separately modeled EOA. It is the user-facing CDP minter bounded by collateral checks and per-market maxSystemDebt and cannot raise its own ceilings.

controls.label: BimaCore governance / parameter admin
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712273, BimaCore.owner()/guardian(), Factory.owner()/guardian(), and BorrowerOperations.owner() still resolved to this code-empty EOA; DebtToken.factory() and borrowerOperationsAddress() remained unchanged and lendingVaultAdapterAddress() remained zero. Verified source gives this owner unbounded authorizedMint, adapter replacement, new TroveManager authorization, and maxSystemDebt raise paths.
controls.capDescription: Unbounded: DebtToken.authorizedMint() has no cap, and this EOA can also raise each collateral maxSystemDebt via TroveManager.setParameters().

controls.label: USBD OFT owner/delegate (deployment-wide EOA)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712273 and Hemi block 5029153, DebtToken.owner() still returned this code-empty EOA. It controls LayerZero OFT peers/delegate configuration and can authorize burn/mint routes across deployments, but native authorizedMint and collateral ceilings remain controlled by the separately modeled BimaCore owner.

controls.label: BIMA Hemi BorrowerOperations (material native CDP minter)
controls.capDescription: Hemi native CDP issuance is bounded by collateral checks and per-market maxSystemDebt; this BorrowerOperations contract cannot raise those limits.
controls.evidence: At Hemi block 5029153, the material Hemi DebtToken returned this BorrowerOperations address and Factory 0xc5790164d3ccb6533b241eee3fd7f56862759376. BorrowerOperations.owner(), Factory.owner(), and BimaCore.owner() all resolved to the separately modeled EOA, while the token's lendingVaultAdapterAddress remained zero.

controls.label: BimaCore Hemi governance / parameter admin
controls.capDescription: Unbounded: the same owner-only authorizedMint, adapter replacement, Factory authorization, and maxSystemDebt parameter paths are deployed on Hemi.
controls.evidence: At Hemi block 5029153, BimaCore.owner()/guardian(), Factory.owner()/guardian(), and BorrowerOperations.owner() all returned this code-empty EOA. The material Hemi deployment therefore has the same unbounded direct-mint and authorization bypass surfaces as Ethereum, with no multisig or timelock.

review.evidence: Fresh reads on 2026-08-08 confirmed the complete shared-address mint path on Ethereum block 25712273 and material Hemi block 5029153. On both deployments, DebtToken 0x6bede1c6009a78c222d9bdb7974bb67847fdb68c returned Factory 0xc5790164d3ccb6533b241eee3fd7f56862759376, BorrowerOperations 0x87fed36c032ee7289a1d2f3c48798e4c7fcdfaec, and a zero lendingVaultAdapterAddress. BimaCore owner/guardian, Factory owner/guardian, and BorrowerOperations owner all resolved to the same code-empty EOA 0xaca5d659364636284041b8d3acad8a57f6e7b8a5; verified source permits that EOA to call uncapped authorizedMint, install a mint-capable adapter, authorize new TroveManagers, and raise per-market maxSystemDebt. DebtToken owner/delegate 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4 is a separate code-empty EOA controlling OFT peers. The contracts are direct deployments with zero EIP-1967 slots. Aggregate mint semantics are unbounded, reconciliation is on-chain/not applicable, no Safe modules or guards apply, and no prudential supervisor was identified.
